items.notes: Lifecycle (candidate/active/corrected/recurring/temporary, confidence, scope isolation) implemented and tested; stale-pattern detection (isPatternStale, 180 days) added earlier. items.title: RLS/security
items.notes: RLS enabled on every table incl. app_config (no client policies, revoked from anon); storage bucket private; prompt-injection defense wrapped into all untrusted doc text; middleware degraded-mode guards regression-tested. SECURITY REGRESSION SUITE (2026-10-05): permanent two-layer privacy gate added to standard acceptance workflow. LIVE matrix tests/security/rls-regression.mjs — real users (OWNER/USER_A/USER_B/UNAUTHORIZED) vs actual RLS: owner NO ACCESS to all nine private categories (assignment, essay, teacher profile, writing samples, feedback, learning patterns, research, typing results, uploaded files); A↔B/anon/revoked/deleted NO ACCESS; owner membership management + aggregate-only analytics verified with zero content markers; fail-closed env (absent→exit 3, partial→exit 1); self-test 4/4 in CI. OFFLINE tests/run.ts §22 (26 assertions, every npm test): all tables RLS-enabled, all policies auth.uid()-scoped, no using(true), network_stats aggregate-only + owner-gated + SECURITY DEFINER, live suite wired into release.yml. Tamper-verified live: removed RLS / permissive policy / analytics content leak each fail the suite. 564/564 tests, build green. No RLS weakened. LIVE run requires owner to set SUPABASE_TEST_* secrets on a disposable test project. INVITATION VERIFICATION (2026-10-05): complete 18-item security verification of the existing invitation-only workflow, no rebuild, no weakening. LIVE tests/security/invitation-regression.mjs: real signUp/trigger/RLS matrix — invitation-refused stranger signup, valid link flow, atomic single-use, expiry, revocation, email binding, missing/fake/modified tokens, owner-only approval, request≠access, removal kills account, zero token leaks (all observed errors mechanically checked against live tokens); fail-closed env; self-test 3/3. OFFLINE tests/run.ts §23 (57 assertions, every npm test): all 18 items verified against actual migration SQL + routes + guard + signup page; tamper-verified T1–T5 (signup-gate bypass, token-lookup loosening, non-atomic claim, dropped owner check, token echo each fail the suite; three loose assertions in the first draft caught and fixed). rls-regression.mjs bootstrap hardened for migration 0008 (owner_email + invitation pre-seed). release.yml runs both live suites when SUPABASE_TEST_* configured. 621/621 tests, build green.

items.title: Assignment-aware source authority: task classification, configurable authority profiles, teacher-override ranking, stored acceptance decisions
items.notes: Added 2026-10-05 as an EXTENSION of research.ts's rankCandidates (which remains untouched and is the generic fallback). classifyAssignment picks history/science/current-events/literature/social-science/general; AUTHORITY_PROFILES hold the configurable tier hierarchies (registerAuthorityProfile replaces a category at runtime); rankCandidatesForAssignment sorts teacher-gate → tier → within-tier score (relevance, evidence quality, date fit). Teacher requirements override generic preferences absolutely. .gov/.edu are never blindly prioritized — institutional domains only count where the profile's hierarchy values them. The per-source decision (tier, flags, reasons) is stored via migration 0014 and surfaced by the citation audit as authority_explanations ('why each source was accepted').
